17.0.s.en: (1) The choosing of the rods and their placing in the Holy of Holies

17.0.0.en: The Lord gave Moses, in speaking with him, a new command, for a reason He will explain to us in (v. 5). This command was to take a rod from each tribe, so that the total of the rods of the tribes was twelve rods. God also commanded that the name of the head of each house, representing his tribe, be written on his rod. It was known that each tribe had a head like those heads who helped in numbering and counting the people, as mentioned in the first chapters of the book.

17.0.1.en: Each of the heads carried a rod as a sign of his headship of the tribe, in addition to using it to lean on. Most likely the rod of Aaron was a branch of an almond tree, as was the custom. Note: the tribes were twelve tribes apart from the tribe of Levi, and so there are two opinions on this matter, which we thought it honest to present:

17.0.2.en: The first opinion: that twelve rods were gathered from the tribes, and the rod of Aaron was the thirteenth for them.

17.0.3.en: The second opinion: that the twelve rods also included the rod of Aaron, and that the tribes of Manasseh and Ephraim shared one rod on which the name of their father Joseph was written.

17.1.0.en: God affirms that Aaron, through his priesthood, became the head and prince of the tribe of Levi, and therefore his name is written on the rod that represents his tribe.

17.2.0.en: God then commanded that all the rods be placed in the Holy of Holies before the ark of the covenant, which contains the two tables of the testimony on which the Ten Commandments are written.

17.2.1.en: Where I will meet with you: that is, in the place before which Moses stands when God speaks to him as a representative of all the people.

17.3.0.en: What God wanted by all this was that He would declare His choice by a miraculous act and a sign at which all would marvel, namely that one rod out of all the rods presented before God would blossom and put forth green leaves or fruit like any living branch not cut from a tree, which is impossible for a dry rod.

17.3.1.en: The rod that budded, in which life stirred after death, would belong to the man whom God chooses, apart from all others, to have the priesthood, he and his descendants alone.

17.3.2.en: I will make to cease from me: I will stop, prevent and nullify the murmurings of the children of Israel.

17.3.3.en: God regarded the murmurings of the people against Moses and Aaron as murmurings against His own blessed person, so He once said “from me” and also said “against you.” God makes clear here that He is a partner with His faithful servant in everything, and in divine humility God regards every insult directed at His servants and priests as directed at His divine self.

17.4.0.en: The heads of the tribes responded to God's request and gave their rods to Moses after their names were engraved on them, and the rod of Aaron joined them. Moses laid all the rods before the Lord as commanded, awaiting what the Lord would declare of His choice of the man set apart for the service of the priesthood.

17.4.1.en: God intervenes to support His children in difficult situations with many kinds of support. He declares His responsibility for the service of His children, to encourage them to serve Him faithfully while He completes what they lack. So be zealous, my brother, for the service of God, that you may experience His work in you and rejoice in His fellowship.

17.5.0.en: Buds: small shoots that grew from the buds.

17.5.1.en: On the very next day Moses went in before the Lord to find himself before a wonderful miracle, for the rod of Aaron had put forth buds and full blossoms and ripened almonds. Moses took all the rods and went out to the heads of the tribes gathered at the door of the tabernacle, and each of them took his own rod, which he knew, with his name engraved on it.

17.5.2.en: In the budding of Aaron's rod many miracles appear:

17.5.3.en: 1- A dry rod cannot give blossoms and fruit, for it is dead and cannot give life after its death.

17.5.4.en: 2- The rod gave branches, buds, blossoms and fruit, which are the different stages of a plant that do not come together at one time but in stages.

17.5.5.en: 3- The choosing of one rod, the rod of Aaron, apart from the rest of the rods.

17.6.0.en: Because Aaron's rod became a symbol of God's miraculous work and a clear sign of His choice of Aaron, Aaron did not take back his rod, but God commanded Moses to keep it in the Holy of Holies, so he placed it inside the ark of the covenant (Heb 9:4), that it might be a permanent sign and testimony before the eyes of the rebellious people, so that they would not return again to their former murmurings or transgressions, and these murmurings would not become a new cause of their destruction.

17.6.1.en: God in His fatherhood to His people and His care for them, despite their many murmurings, wished to give them a memorial so that they would not return to their evil and He would be compelled to punish them... Do you too keep memorials of God's works in your life, so that you do not forget His kindnesses and give thanks for them?... How evil it is for a man to forget and murmur, so that his punishment is great. And remember, my brother, that a man's pride and constant discontent are behind the sin of murmuring and what it brings upon him.

17.7.0.en: Moses carried out the Lord's command and left Aaron's rod in the Holy of Holies.

17.8.0.en: Feelings of fear mingled with grief and regret among the people, and the people spoke, broken before the death and destruction that had come on Korah, Dathan and Abiram, those who followed them in the rebellion, and those whom the plague destroyed afterward. They offered repentance before God and said that they had learned a hard lesson, the price of which was that we were all exposed to perishing, and this lesson is that we should not stand again before the house of the Lord, for everyone who comes near this tabernacle with boldness and rebellion, like Korah and the two hundred and fifty men, perishes utterly. The people said this in grief and brokenness, but what they uttered was also far from the reality, because destruction did not come on one who wished to stand before the house of the Lord, but on the few who murmured against God and His priesthood and wanted the priesthood to belong to all, thereby breaking what God Himself had ordained. As this chapter ends, we wish to pause a little before the miracle of Aaron's rod, for the meanings and symbols it carries:

17.8.1.en: 1- The Incarnation: Aaron's rod first signifies Christ, for He is the life that came out of the dry ground (the Jewish people), as Isaiah prophesied and said, “For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground”

17.8.2.en: (Isa 53:2), that is, the Incarnation of Christ and the appearing of God from the midst of humanity condemned to death.

17.8.3.en: 2- The Cross: for the Cross is the dry wood that gives life to everyone who holds fast to it, since in it is the power of the crucified Redeemer.

17.8.4.en: 3- The Resurrection of Christ: where Christ rose alive from the dead like the budding of the dead rod.

17.8.5.en: 4- The coming forth of life from the dry wood is an indication of the Gentiles' acceptance of the faith, for the living faith came forth from dead idolatry.

17.8.6.en: 5- Aaron's rod also signifies the Virgin Lady, who without any human planting, sowing or watering conceived and bore the Son of God, the Word incarnate, and for this reason we pray in the Midnight Praise and say, “What is the rod but Mary, for she is the type of her virginity..”

17.8.7.en: 6- The coming forth of life from death fills our hearts with hope when facing difficult and distant souls, for how many souls were dry and refusing and became believers, even fruitful servants in the Church of God.

17.8.8.en: Introduction to the obligations and rights of the priests and Levites: This chapter moves us to the priests and the Levites. It speaks in general about their responsibilities in guarding the tabernacle, that is, the house of God, then speaks about the material rights of the priests and Levites, and the obligation to pay the tithes of the Levites and the priests.

18.0.s.en: (1) The duties of the priests and Levites

18.0.0.en: Shall bear the iniquity: you will bear the results of your faults before Me and their consequences.

18.0.1.en: This time God spoke with Aaron directly, as high priest, because all the speech concerns him and the Levites with him. The beginning of the speech with him was decisive, for God reminds him of his basic and important responsibility. He and all his descendants after him have become responsible directly before Him for two things:

18.0.2.en: First: the sanctuary. This means their responsibility to oversee all the affairs of the service in the house, inside and outside, such as cleanliness and order, preventing anyone of the people from touching the holy things, and also keeping all the ordinances and rites as the Lord delivered them to Moses and Aaron.

18.0.3.en: Second: your priesthood. The responsibility also includes their keeping watch over their conduct and being careful in all they do, so that no stumbling block comes to the people from their shepherds and leaders. The expression “shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood” is an expression that carries the form of a warning more than the form of counsel or guidance.

18.0.4.en: In sum, they are responsible for:

18.0.5.en: 1- Guarding all the contents of the house of the Lord.

18.0.6.en: 2- Being careful in offering worship according to the commands of the Law.

18.0.7.en: 3- Guiding the people and preventing them from wrong against the house of the Lord.

18.0.8.en: 4- The good conduct of the priests, that they may be an example to the people in their relationship with God and in their whole life.

18.1.0.en: God also charges Aaron, who represents the priesthood, not to be proud toward the rest of the Levites of his tribe, who signify the deacons, but that the relationship between them be a relationship of connection, support and completeness. For the service in the end is one service in its two parts, whether the priesthood or the service of keeping and carrying. This teaches us that in the service, regardless of the difference of our positions, each of us needs the other.

18.2.0.en: The Levites likewise are to be a guard and protection for Aaron in his own person and for his priestly descendants after him against any assault or attack by the people, and they also guard the whole tabernacle against any intrusion or damage. But they must also know their limits and not transgress them by entering the sanctuary or the Holy of Holies or touching any of the vessels of the service, lest both Levites and priests be exposed to the penalty of death for transgressing what God ordained for the affairs of the service and the determination of duties within the tabernacle.

18.3.0.en: The stranger: that is, anyone of the common people other than the tribe of Levi.

18.3.1.en: God repeats and affirms to Aaron what He had said before, to show all the seriousness of the matter. He adds here that one of the tasks of the Levites is also that no individual of the people other than the tribe of Levi come near the tabernacle, otherwise the divine wrath would include the whole people of the children of Israel. God also repeats that the care and service of the outer and the inner altar belong to the priests alone.

18.4.0.en: God repeats for the third time what He had said, which increases the awe of this matter on the soul, but this time He adds something new and shows us a new spiritual concept, that God is the One who chooses His servants by His grace and calls them to serve His vineyard, that is, His Church. So the Levites gained a special honor and a distinguished position. Because of the distinction and majesty of the priestly service, God gave the Levites to the priests as helpers, but the priests must also care for the dignity of the grace they have received, “keep your priesthood,” and this means:

18.4.1.en: a) Caring for the ritual worship as God delivered it to them.

18.4.2.en: b) Caring for their own life and general conduct, for they are an example to all the people.

18.4.3.en: c) That no one other than the priests enter the sanctuary, and no one other than the high priest enter the Holy of Holies, which is beyond the veil.

18.4.4.en: My beloved brother, you may be a servant or a deacon whom God has called to serve His house. Do you realize the measure of this honor and this calling? Do you also care for your service and not neglect or treat it lightly? Do you keep all that God ordained or the Church established of rites and order of worship? You are responsible before God, so do not forget this!!!

18.5.s.en: (2) The priests' rights from the offerings of the people

18.5.0.en: The charge of mine heave offerings: a portion of the sacrifices offered to My name, for the heave offering is the sacrifice lifted up to God.

18.5.1.en: By reason of the anointing: that is, as a wage and portion for the service of the priesthood.

18.5.2.en: God speaks here with Aaron and shows His care for every servant who serves Him. He says to him: I have given and granted you, that is, all the priests, portions of the sacrifices offered to Me and to My name from all the offerings of the children of Israel, whether vows or sacrifices required to be offered. It is as if God wished to say to the priests: in return for your service and your consecration to Me, you have become partners of My table and you eat from My portion that is offered to Me.

18.6.0.en: This shall be thine of the most holy things: an expression meaning that what you will receive is considered most holy, since you will eat of what is offered to the Lord Himself.

18.6.1.en: Heave offerings: everything lifted up from the sacrifice to be offered to God, which is the breast and the right shoulder (Ex 29:28). The right of the anointing: the right of the anointing of the priesthood, that is, the rights of the priests.

18.6.2.en: The priests have a portion of all the offerings presented to the fire of the altar, whether sin offerings or trespass offerings offered to God, and it becomes a holy portion and due for them and for all their generations. The details of this came in the book of Leviticus (ch. 4-7).

18.7.0.en: In the most holy place shalt thou eat it: of course what is meant here is not the place of the Holy of Holies, which it is forbidden to enter except once a year on the Day of Atonement and by the high priest alone, but eating it in a clean and holy place. The usual place where the priests ate of the sacrifices was the outer court of the house of the Lord, and those who ate of these sacrifices were the priests and their male children only.

18.7.1.en: It shall be holy unto thee: that is, it shall become a portion for you.

18.8.0.en: From the sacrifices there were other portions that the priests took to their homes for their women to eat, which are some parts of the peace offerings, such as the shoulder of the sacrifice or its breast, which were offered by “waving” before the Lord. The divine inspiration added the words “by a statute for ever” to be sure that this applied to the whole line of the priesthood throughout the days, as long as the Levitical priesthood stood, and was not limited to Aaron and his family.

18.9.2.en: The portions of the priests also included “all the best,” that is, the best of what is offered of oil, wine or grains of wheat from the firstfruits of the people. Everyone who offered his firstfruits to the Lord, the Lord gave them to His priests. These firstfruits also included the fruits and produce of the land, which the priest takes to his house to eat with his family.

18.10.0.en: Every thing devoted in Israel: the devoted thing is what a man forbade to himself and gave to the Lord in the form of a vow or property or the like, and every devoted thing becomes the portion of the priests.

18.11.0.en: The firstborn of man and of animals were offered to God, as is stated in (Ex 13). God replaced the firstborn of men with the tribe of the Levites and chose them for service and consecration. If the number of the firstborn exceeded the number of the Levites, the firstborn was redeemed with a sum of money of five shekels of silver, or a hundred gerahs, because the shekel is 20 gerahs (see ch. 3:46). The firstborn of all clean animals was given to the priests, while the firstborn of unclean animals, such as the ass, had its blood not brought to the altar, but its offering was replaced with another offering, such as a sheep, and if it was not redeemed it had to be killed.

18.12.0.en: But the firstborn of clean animals, such as cattle, sheep or goats, must be offered, and nothing can be offered in place of them, because they are set apart and chosen by the Lord, that is, He set them apart and hallowed them for Himself, so they cannot be replaced, but their blood and fat must be offered on the altar for a sweet savour as the Lord commanded, while the flesh belongs to the priests. This is like what happens with the portions that God had previously fixed for them, such as the heave shoulder and the wave breast, which were spoken of before.

18.12.1.en: If God cared for the priests and the details of their material needs because they consecrated their lives to His service, be sure that you too, if you are bound to Christ and His service, He will care for all your needs and will not forsake you.

18.13.0.en: A covenant of salt: that is, an everlasting covenant.

18.13.1.en: To thee and to thy seed: that is, to the priests and their descendants.

18.13.2.en: As a final review of all that preceded, God repeats to Aaron and his sons that all the portions, vows, offerings and sacrifices, except the burnt offering, that are offered to the Lord, the Lord in turn gives to the priests after the sprinkling of the blood around the altar and after the burning of their fat, and the priests eat them with their households all the days.

18.14.0.en: God affirms to Aaron that he will have no fixed portion in the land like the rest of the tribes, because God will be his portion and in place of everything. The beautiful spiritual meaning is that whoever leaves anything for the sake of God possesses everything in return, since the Lord has become his portion, as St. Paul mentioned and said, “as having nothing, and yet possessing all things” (2 Cor 6:10).

18.15.0.en: After God spoke about the portions of the priests from the offerings and sacrifices, His speech turned to the Levites also, the servants of the tabernacle of the congregation, and God established for them the tithes of the income of all the people, from their produce and the profits of their trade, after they dwell in the land. If the priests take the firstfruits, the Levites take the tithes.

18.16.0.en: They shall bear their iniquity: they bear their responsibility and the results of any failure in it.

18.16.1.en: God warns all the people not to come near the tabernacle of the congregation and touch anything of its contents, otherwise they will be exposed to death. Those allowed to serve the house of God are only the Levites, because they know how to fulfill the Law of God, and any breach of it brings God's punishment on them. This service is assigned to the Levites throughout the generations until Christ comes. The Levites possess no inheritance in the Promised Land, because God is their inheritance, like the priests.

18.17.0.en: Heave offering: lifted up and offered to the Lord.

18.17.1.en: This verse comes as a confirmation and review of what was said before in verses 21-23, the sum of which is that the tithes the people give to the Levites are offered to God Himself.

18.17.2.en: Know that everything you have is a gift from God, so before you use it, may you receive God's blessing by offering a part of it, which is the tithe, and be sure that the rest, by God's blessing, will be enough for your needs, however narrow your financial circumstances. “The blessing of the LORD, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it” (Prov 10:22).

18.18.0.en: Ye shall offer up: you shall present.

18.18.1.en: God's speech here is to the Levites also, telling them through Moses that just as they received tithes from the people and their houses were filled with good things, so they too must offer to the Lord their tithes. The Levites are not excepted from the tithes here, for God wishes to teach them that He gives to all and is the maker of good things, and that as a man rejoiced in receiving, so he must rejoice in giving.

18.19.2.en: The threshingfloor: the floor, which is the place where the grain is separated from the husk and stored.

18.19.3.en: The fulness: what fills the vessel to its brim.

18.19.4.en: As the people offer from their tithes the grain that is in the threshingfloor and the oil and wine that are in the winepress, so also the Levites offer a tenth of what they took from the people and give it to the priests in the person of Aaron. That is, if the Levites receive the tenth, the priests take 1/100 of the produce of the people.

18.20.0.en: The best thereof, the hallowed part: the best of the good things and offerings.

18.20.1.en: God affirms what He said before and asks the Levites that the tithes they will offer must be of the best that can be offered, because the offering is offered to God Himself and He gives it to His priests.

18.21.0.en: He asks Moses to tell them that when they do this and offer the best they have, God regards it as the fruit of their labors, and this is a repetition of what came in (v. 27), so God blesses the remaining nine tenths with the Levites.

18.22.0.en: The speech here is about the nine tenths remaining with the Levites, for God blesses them for them and wishes them to enjoy them with their families, since He fully appreciates their labor in the service of the tabernacle, in taking it down, carrying it and setting it up.

18.23.1.en: When you offer the tithe, “the best thereof,” from your portion, you will be justified before God and will bear no sin or guilt, for if you do otherwise you defile the offerings of the children of Israel offered to My own self, and thus expose your souls to punishment and death.

18.23.2.en: My beloved brother... it is not enough to give tithes to God, but you must also give the best that you have and not the least or most despised of it. For what you give to any man you give to God Himself in the person of this man... Would God, then, be given the lesser, the worse and the stale!!!

18.23.3.en: Introduction to the law of the red heifer: This chapter is connected with what came in the book of Leviticus (ch. 11, ch. 21). If the book of Leviticus spoke of the uncleanness of one who touches the dead and the necessity of his purification before dealing with or touching anyone, the book of Numbers in this chapter presents the law of purification through the sacrifice of the red heifer, whose law we shall come to know in detail.
